question: Which of the following metals is most likely to be found in the free state in nature due to its low reactivity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gold** is one of the **least reactive metals**, which means it does not easily form compounds with other elements. This property allows gold to exist in its free state in nature.
 
• Gold has very low reactivity because it is placed at the bottom of the **reactivity series of metals**. It does not react with oxygen, water, or acids under standard conditions.
 
• Due to its inert nature, gold is found in nature primarily as **native gold**, often mixed with quartz or other minerals, rather than as compounds.
 
• Other metals such as **iron, zinc, and copper** are more reactive compared to gold. These metals are typically found as ores combined with oxygen, sulfur, or other elements.
 
• Gold’s unique chemical properties make it highly valuable and desirable for applications such as **jewelry, electronics, and investment** purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iron:**

 
 
• Iron is a highly reactive metal and is usually found in nature as iron ores such as **hematite** (Fe₂O₃) and **magnetite** (Fe₃O₄).
 
• It reacts with oxygen and water, forming **iron oxides** such as rust under normal conditions.
 
• Iron is primarily used in construction, machinery, and as a key component in **steel production**.
 
 
 
• **Zinc:**
 
 
• Zinc is moderately reactive and is usually found as zinc ores like **zinc blende** (ZnS) or **calamine** (ZnCO₃).
 
• It reacts with acids and alkalis, releasing hydrogen gas.
 
• Zinc is widely used in galvanization, batteries, and alloys such as **brass**.
 
 
 
• **Copper:**
 
 
• Copper is less reactive than iron and zinc but more reactive than gold. It is often found as **malachite** (CuCO₃.Cu(OH)₂) and other ores.
 
• Copper reacts with oxygen at high temperatures, forming copper oxide.
 
• Due to its excellent electrical conductivity, copper is widely used in **electrical wiring** and electronics.
 
 
 
• **Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is found in nature in its native form as nuggets or grains in rocks and alluvial deposits.
 
• It does not corrode or tarnish even after prolonged exposure to air and water.
 
• Gold’s rarity and inertness make it a preferred choice for **jewelry, currency reserves, and electronics.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The **reactivity series** ranks metals based on their reactivity with water, acids, and oxygen.
 
• Gold is at the bottom of the series, indicating its **low reactivity**. Metals like potassium, sodium, and calcium are at the top, showing high reactivity.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is used in **electronics** due to its excellent conductivity and resistance to corrosion.
 
• It serves as a reliable investment option and is stored in the form of **bullion** or coins.
 
• Gold is widely used in **dentistry** and medicine for its biocompatibility.
 
 
 
• **Extraction of Gold:**
 
 
• Gold is extracted using methods such as **panning, sluicing, and cyanidation**.
 
• Cyanidation involves dissolving gold in a cyanide solution to separate it from impurities.
